alt: A collage showing three Uber app screenshots detailing a delivery ride and an Uber Support email regarding a reported incident.
summary:
The image displays three Uber application screenshots and one Uber Support email. The first Uber screen shows "Ride details" for a "Courier ride with JOEL" on Feb 9, 2026, at 10:23 PM, costing $110.79, with identical pickup and dropoff addresses at 9801 Airport Blvd, Los Angeles, CA 90045, US. The second screen is an Uber receipt for Nicolas, dated Feb 9, 2026, 10:23 PM, totaling $110.79, with a delivery fare of $95.33 and a booking fee of $15.46, paid via Uber Cash ($77.88) and Visa ($32.91). The third Uber screen shows "Trip details" for a "Courier" trip, stating "50.00 miles, 10 min" and "Delivered by JOEL," with a map showing a short, direct route.

The fourth image is a Gmail screenshot showing an Uber Support email titled "Report a serious incident with a driver." The email, dated "Monday, February 9, 2026 at 10:23:56 PM," thanks Nicolas for getting in touch but states, "We can confirm that the time frame to review this trip has passed. Only trips completed less than 30 days ago can be reviewed." It advises reaching out sooner in the future.

Several discrepancies are evident. All Uber documents are dated February 9, 2026, which is in the future, suggesting the documents are fabricated or for a test. The "Trip details" claim a "50.00 miles, 10 min" journey, which is physically impossible, especially given the map showing a very short distance and the pickup/dropoff times indicating a 5-minute duration (10:29 PM to 10:34 PM). Furthermore, the pickup and dropoff addresses are identical, which is unusual for a delivery. The Uber Support email, while dated the same day as the trip (Feb 9, 2026), states that the 30-day review window has passed, creating a logical contradiction. The Gmail timestamp of "1:03 AM (29 minutes ago)" implies the email was viewed on Feb 10, 2026, but the content refers to a past event beyond the 30-day window, despite the email's own date being concurrent with the trip. These inconsistencies strongly suggest the documents are not authentic records of a real-world event.
